issues.title: Advertise relay identity and jurisdiction in SETUP
issues.author: cisco-sbg-altanai
issues.body:
## Motivation
Sovereign deployments and geofencing need a peer to identify the relay it connected to and evaluate that relay jurisdiction before media is routed. The current draft mixes static identity and changing metrics, and its identity example combines multiple geocode forms.

## Desired outcome
Specify a relay-only GEOCODE_IDENTITY Setup Option with a stable relay ID, exactly one primary geocode representation, explicit jurisdiction fields, and a stated location precision. Clarify that each relay advertises only its own claim and that the claim requires an operator trust process for compliance use.

## Reason for the change
A direct peer needs the relay jurisdiction during session setup; a controller needs trustworthy jurisdiction claims to reject routes that cross a prohibited boundary. Dynamic metrics need a refreshable track rather than setup-time values.

issues.title: Specify client geofence intent and relay handover
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
## Motivation
A sovereign-deployment client needs to state its own jurisdiction policy and desired relay proximity when connecting. The current draft does not explain how a relay responds when the connected relay cannot satisfy that policy.

## Desired outcome
Define a GEOCODE_INTENT Setup Option for allowed jurisdictions and an optional near_me preference that does not require client coordinates. Specify authorization checks and how a relay moves a session or request to a compliant relay using the applicable MOQT GOAWAY or REDIRECT behavior.

## Reason for the change
The client owns the policy decision. An initial relay must be able to evaluate that intent, select or hand over to an eligible relay, and fail closed when a strict jurisdiction policy cannot be met. Authentication and authorization must guard both intent and location disclosure.

issues.title: Record hop-by-hop path events and relay metrics
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
Reason: sovereignty and geofencing decisions need evidence about the relay path actually used, while operators need diagnostics to understand delivery behavior.

Desired outcome: define a hop-by-hop path event for each forwarded Object, correlated to that Object, with relay identity, ingress and egress peers, forwarding direction, relay geocode, timestamp, ingress and egress SRTT observations, Object received bytes, and a cumulative connection byte counter with an epoch/reset indication. Keep dynamic metrics and path events on discoverable tracks rather than in SETUP, and do not modify the Object, its Properties, or payload. Make telemetry optional and subject to authorization and privacy policy. Treat disagreement between measured SRTT and geographic distance as an anomaly signal for investigation, not proof of location or misconduct.

Why: a relay's advertised location alone does not show which relays handled traffic, how much data each hop received, or whether the observed path is consistent with the client's policy. Per-hop evidence supports geofence auditing, operational diagnostics, and informed handover while preserving the media object.

pulls.title: Clarify relay geocode, geofencing, and hop-by-hop evidence
pulls.author: altanai
pulls.body:
## Summary

- Advertise each relay's own identity and geocode in its SETUP message, using either WGS84 or IATA plus an explicit jurisdiction claim.
- Add client geofence and proximity intent for sovereignty use cases, with authorization checks and relay handover through MOQT session migration or request redirection.
- Put changing metrics and per-Object, hop-by-hop path events on dedicated tracks. Include ingress/egress peers, direction, relay geocode, timestamps, per-hop SRTT, bytes received, and a cumulative counter with an epoch. Do not modify Objects, Object Properties, payloads, or extension headers.
- Specify network JSON as UTF-8 per RFC 8259 and clarify trust, privacy, and the limits of SRTT/geocode comparison.

Related issues: #1, #2, #3.

pulls.title: Specify relay geocode identity in SETUP
pulls.author: altanai
pulls.body:
Addresses issue #5: define the relay identity and jurisdiction claim, use one WGS84 or IATA geocode, state the location precision, and clarify UTF-8 JSON/SETUP framing.

MOQT references are updated to v23. Factual review confirms SETUP extensions are extensible and unknown options are ignored.

pulls.title: Add client geofence intent and relay handover
pulls.author: altanai
pulls.body: Addresses issue #2: let clients state location intent and geofencing policy, including a requested relay proximity, while keeping authorization and policy enforcement with the client/deployment. Handover uses MOQT v23 session or request migration semantics.

pulls.title: Add hop-by-hop path events and relay metrics
pulls.author: altanai
pulls.body: Addresses issue #3: describe immutable per-hop path events, dynamic metrics, per-adjacent-connection SRTT, cumulative received bytes with an epoch, and hop-by-hop relay geocode. Keep media Objects and the transport extension header unchanged; use a dedicated metrics track for evolving data. Factual review corrected stale text that suggested sending changing metrics in SETUP.
